clue.text: Become stupid — in short, romantic

parts.note: to go is to become, as in go bald or go mad

indicators.note: in short says the word for stupid is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: thick is informal for stupid

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a romantic outlook is making a person dim-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Become stupid' is GO THICK; 'in short' drops the last K. Gothic is the romantic style of brooding novels and ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic describes the Romantic-era literary taste for gloomy castles, mystery and the supernatural.

clue.text: Old performer encountered coming in with 'lengthy' instrument

indicators.note: coming in means the word for encountered goes inside the word for performer

parts.note: a doer is one who performs, does things
met means encountered

explanation.surface: An old actor met someone arriving with a long musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lengthy' is in quotes because the instrument measures length, the distance a vehicle covers.
explanation.definitionFit: An odometer is a device in a vehicle recording distance travelled.

clue.text: Tradition handed down from their peculiar era

indicators.note: peculiar means strange, so the letters of their come out oddly arranged

parts.note: an age is an era

explanation.surface: A custom passed on from a strange period in history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peculiar' stands between the two words but works only on the one before it; 'era' is not fodder but a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Heritage is what is inherited from the past: customs, buildings, culture.

clue.text: Plant, black one in vertical line with little energy

indicators.note: in means the letters for black and one go inside the word for a vertical line

parts.note: a column is a vertical line, as in a column of figures
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
I is one in Roman numerals
E is the physics symbol for energy, a little or short form

explanation.surface: A gardener's note on a plant set in a straight row, needing little effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Columbine is the garden flower also called aquilegia.

clue.text: Suffer in isolation much less

parts.note: to suffer in the old sense is to allow or permit, to let
alone means on one's own, in isolation

explanation.surface: Someone endures their troubles in solitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffer' looks like enduring pain; here it is the archaic 'permit' (Suffer the little children).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces something even less likely, as in he can't walk, never mind run.

clue.text: Significant, like the 0 of 3,2,1,0? No!

parts.note: zero ends a countdown, so it comes at the end; it is also the smallest number, but the clue says no to that and insists on importance

explanation.surface: A puzzle about whether zero in a countdown really matters.
explanation.walkthrough: In a launch countdown zero is final and lowest; the phrase denies the lowness while keeping the finality.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a final item while stressing it is just as important as the rest.

clue.text: Money handed out after the match is over

definitions.text: Money handed out after the match is over

parts.words: Money handed out after the match is over
parts.note: the match is a marriage, not a sporting fixture, and the payment follows a divorce

explanation.surface: Prize money is paid once the game has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' reads as a sporting contest; it is a marriage, so 'over' means divorced.
explanation.definitionFit: Payments made by one former spouse to the other after a divorce or separation.

clue.text: Permissive one in platoon out of order

indicators.note: in means the letter for one is placed among the letters of platoon
out of order means jumbled, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A lenient soldier in a platoon is behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' looks like misconduct; it is the anagram signal for I plus PLATOON.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left optional is allowed but not required, a matter of choice.

clue.text: Savage is serene, conveying a spooky quality

indicators.note: savage means violent and wild, so the letters of is serene are violently disordered

explanation.surface: A savage beast that appears calm gives off something unsettling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Savage' poses as a noun; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eeriness is weirdness that makes one uneasy, an uncanny feeling.

clue.text: Like a basic package implying a lack of excitement for cockney

parts.note: no means none, a lack of

indicators.note: a cockney speaker famously says F for TH, so the word for excitement has its opening pair swapped for F

parts.note: thrills are excitement

explanation.surface: A cheap holiday deal promises little excitement to a Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney (East London) speech turns 'th' into 'f', so 'thrills' becomes 'frills'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain, budget offer has nothing extra or decorative added.

clue.text: Boy of six about to visit Dartmoor hill?

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
c is short for circa, about
a tor is a rocky hilltop, typical of Dartmoor in Devon

explanation.surface: A six-year-old lad is about to go and see a hill on Dartmoor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'going to'; 'about' is C and 'to visit' just places it before TOR. Dartmoor is a moorland in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor is a boy's name.

clue.text: Unfriendly horde disturbing boatmen by river

indicators.note: disturbing means the letters of boatmen are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A hostile crowd harasses the men in boats along a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent-a-mob is a hired or ready-made crowd of protesters, often aggressive.

clue.text: Clown performing in cloak

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown
on means performing, as in on stage

explanation.surface: A clown does his act wearing a cape.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown was a celebrated British circus clown. 'Cloak' is a verb here: to wrap up.
explanation.definitionFit: To cocoon something is to wrap it up snugly and protectively, to envelop it.

clue.text: Showy rubbish collected by non-U guy

indicators.note: collected by means taken inside, held by the other letters
non-U says the letter U is removed from the word guy

parts.note: litter is rubbish dropped about

explanation.surface: A flashy fellow of the wrong class picks up the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' is old British slang for not upper-class; here it simply means 'take away U', and 'collected by' puts the rubbish inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittery things sparkle and catch the eye, flashy rather than subtle.

clue.text: Signal to stop performance? It's needed if the script's poor

definitions.text: It's needed if the script's poor

parts.note: a red light is the signal to stop
action means performance, doing something

explanation.surface: A director halts a scene that is going badly because of bad writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Script' suggests a film; the definition means a poor piece of writing needing editing.
explanation.definitionFit: Redaction is editing or censoring text, which badly written copy calls for.

clue.text: North American Indian, 100, about last of tribe

parts.note: C is 100 in Roman numerals
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word tribe

explanation.surface: A hundred people gather around the last member of a tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cree are a First Nations people of Canada and the northern US.

clue.text: Plume of feathers around central shape

indicators.note: around means the word for plume goes round the abbreviation for central

parts.note: a crest is a tuft or plume of feathers on a bird's head
cen is an abbreviation for central

explanation.surface: A tuft of feathers circles a central shape, like a helmet emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescent is the curved outline of a waxing or waning moon.

clue.text: I'm 'ere with an X — if you get it all wrong!

definitions.text: I'm 'ere with an X — if you get it all wrong!

indicators.note: wrong means these letters are put in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A marker, speaking cockney, announces they are here with a cross for every mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of I'M 'ERE AN X spells the answer, and the whole clue describes someone who marks errors with a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who marks an exam puts a cross by wrong answers.

clue.text: Mountains showing some displacement to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left
some means only a part of the word displacement is used

explanation.surface: Mountains show a little movement westwards, like drifting continents.
explanation.walkthrough: SPLA sits inside displacement; read westward it gives the European range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are the great mountain range of central Europe.

clue.text: A marine, our lad, equipped to go into battle

parts.note: RM stands for Royal Marine
taken as written
Ed is a short name for a boy, a lad

explanation.surface: A Marine described as one of our boys is kitted out for combat.
explanation.walkthrough: RM is Royal Marines, the British navy's soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Armoured means protected with steel plating, ready for fighting.

clue.text: Metal in lever is absolutely pure

indicators.note: in means the word for metal goes inside the word for lever

parts.note: to prise is to lever, force open
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Metal inside a lever has not a trace of impurity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lever' is a verb here: PRISE, as in prise open a lid.
explanation.definitionFit: Pristine means in original, unspoiled condition, spotless.

clue.text: Instrument that gives something a second binding?

definitions.text: that gives something a second binding?

explanation.surface: A device for tying things up a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as RE-CORDER: one who cords (binds with rope) again.
explanation.definitionFit: A recorder is a woodwind instrument; jokingly, a re-corder ties with cord once more.

clue.text: More than one old widow starts to recollect each little interesting curiosity they've seen

indicators.note: starts to means take the first letter of each of the following words

parts.words: recollect each little interesting curiosity they've seen

explanation.surface: Elderly widows love to recall every small curious thing they've witnessed.
explanation.walkthrough: Relict is an archaic word for a widow.
explanation.definitionFit: Relict is an old legal or literary term for a surviving spouse.

clue.text: Society takes hint unreservedly

parts.note: to imply is to hint

explanation.surface: A social club picks up on a suggestion with no hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Simply can mean absolutely or completely, as in simply wonderful.

clue.text: Game makes the French angry (against English)

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
cross means angry

explanation.surface: A game that annoys the French when they play England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' just means next to, putting E at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks.

clue.text: Woman giving brief view as a Brussels fan?

parts.note: Brussels is home of the EU, the European Union
a short opinion, a verdict in one word such as nice

explanation.surface: A woman offers a quick opinion as a supporter of the European project.
explanation.walkthrough: A fan of Brussels would say the EU is nice, a brief verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunice is a woman's name.

clue.text: Impure water in a channel islands duct

parts.note: a drain is a duct for water

explanation.surface: Dirty water collects in a drainpipe on Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands (Jersey, Guernsey and others) lie off the French coast and belong to the British Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain is precipitation polluted by industrial emissions.

clue.text: Attends and switches off

explanation.definitionFit: To turn out is to show up at an event; to turn out the lights is to switch them off.

clue.text: Northern stranger who may be falling asleep?

parts.note: odder means stranger, more peculiar

explanation.surface: An eccentric northerner keeps dozing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun (an unknown person); it is the comparative adjective, odder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dropping off to sleep lets their head nod forward.
